chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The milk is the food of the sent (Prophets).
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of milk in Shia Islamic tradition according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) designates milk as the 'food of the Messengers,' linking its consumption to the dietary habits of Prophets like Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) and emphasizing its natural purity (fitrah). In Shia jurisprudence, this narration underscores the virtue of milk as a wholesome, easily digestible sustenance, often cited to support its status as a pure (tahir) and beneficial food for both physical health and spiritual clarity.
